title: Income tax reassessment - the time limits after recent legal changes
p1: Think your old income tax returns can be reopened anytime? Many taxpayers believe the tax department has unlimited power to reassess past years — but that is not true.
p2: A lesser-known fact is that recent legal changes have introduced clearer boundaries for reassessment. The time limit depends on factors like the amount of escaped income and the specific circumstances of the case. In many situations, reassessment cannot go back endlessly into the past.
p3: In simple terms, reassessment is a process where the tax department reviews an earlier return if it believes some income was missed. The law now focuses on giving authorities enough time to act while also protecting taxpayers from indefinite uncertainty. For individuals and businesses, keeping records of income, expenses, and tax filings becomes even more important because old transactions may still matter within the permitted period.
conclusion: Did you know that income tax reassessment has specific time limits, or did you assume the tax department could reopen returns from any year?
